input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Console idle and stale resource reports

## Description

Deliver idle and stale resource reporting in the RHOAI web console: a
per-project idle-workbench report and a stale pipeline-run report, each
exportable as CSV. Cluster administrators get a single place to see which
resources are sitting idle — workbenches nobody has touched in weeks that keep
their volumes and reservations, and old completed pipeline runs accumulating
storage — so they can reclaim capacity with confidence. No new backend data
collection is built: the reports surface data the platform already tracks
(notebook-controller last-activity timestamps and Kubeflow Pipelines run
completion metadata).

## Scope

- Add a per-project idle-workbench report to the web console showing, for each
  workbench: last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking), owner, and reserved resources (volumes, reservations).
- Add a stale pipeline-run report to the web console showing completed
  pipeline runs older than a configurable age, with their retained artifacts,
  sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Implement the configurable age threshold for the stale-run report (default
  value is an implementation decision for the team).
- Implement CSV export of either report (administrators can export the
  idle-workbench report or the stale pipeline-run report).
- Surface both reports in the console's existing project-scoped navigation and
  views, consistent with how the console already lists workbenches and pipeline
  runs.
- Verify the passive data sources as part of this work (no code changes in
  those components — see Acceptance Criteria).

Out of scope: automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources, and
cost/chargeback calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with workbenches of varying activity, when an administrator
  opens the idle-workbench report, then each workbench is listed with its last
  activity, owner, and reserved resources, and the last-activity values match
  the notebook controller's per-kernel activity tracking (validated against
  the culler's view of the same workbenches).
- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of varying age, when an
  administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report with a configured age
  threshold, then only completed runs older than the threshold are listed,
  together with their retained artifacts, and the run completion metadata
  matches what Kubeflow Pipelines reports through its v2 API for the same
  project.
- Given either report is displayed, when the administrator triggers CSV
  export, then a CSV file is produced containing the report's rows and
  columns.
- Given a different age threshold is configured, when the stale pipeline-run
  report is reloaded, then the report reflects the new threshold without a
  console redeployment.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from notebook controller activity tracking.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of either report — bundled because it is a
  presentation mode of the same report views and shares their data structures
  and UI surface; it is not independently schedulable from the reports
  themselves.

# Document idle resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

Author user-facing documentation for the idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run
reports delivered by this strategy: what each report shows, where to find it in
the RHOAI web console, how to interpret last-activity and staleness data, and
the safe manual steps administrators can take to reclaim capacity from idle
resources. Documentation of reclamation covers manual, admin-driven steps
only — automated reclamation is out of scope for this strategy.

## Scope

- New documentation topics explaining the per-project idle-workbench report:
  columns (last activity, owner, reserved resources), data source, and how to
  read it.
- New documentation topics explaining the stale pipeline-run report: the
  configurable age threshold, retained artifacts, and how to configure the
  threshold.
- Documentation of CSV export for both reports.
- A safe-reclamation guide: the manual steps an administrator follows to
  reclaim capacity from idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, with
  cautions about data that is lost when resources are reclaimed.
- Content follows the Red Hat docs content process and tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics exist covering both reports, their columns and data
  sources, the configurable age threshold, and CSV export.
- A safe-reclamation procedure is documented, including cautions for actions
  that permanently remove data (volume deletion, artifact cleanup).
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports
  and accurately reflects the shipped behavior (column names, navigation
  location, configuration mechanism).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016

Idle resource reporting in the web console.

## Triage

Not below-threshold: the strategy spans three components (web console reading
from two architecturally distinct backend data sources — the notebook
controller's activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata) and includes
a substantive documentation work stream (HLR-4 authors new doc topics, not
incidental touch-ups). Not docs-only: the RHOAI web console requires code
changes. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Console idle and stale resource reports | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Document idle resource reports and safe reclamation | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P2 |

## Component Analysis

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Classification | Handling |
|--------------------|---------------------|----------------|----------|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | Active (code changes: new report views + CSV export) | Epic RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Passive (no code changes — last-activity data already tracked per kernel) | Validation acceptance criteria on RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Passive (no code changes — run completion metadata already retained) | Validation acceptance criteria on RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 |

Component mappings (all verbatim from `.context/rhai-components.txt`):
"RHOAI web console" → `Dashboard`; "Notebook controller" → `Notebooks`;
"Kubeflow Pipelines" → `Data Science Pipelines`. The passive components are
validated by the implementing Dashboard team (both surface data through
existing Kubernetes CRs / the KFP v2 REST API the Dashboard already reads), so
no separate validation epics are generated.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 --> RHAISTRAT-9016-E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 → RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring always last) | The documentation describes the reports and reclamation steps that the implementation epic delivers; it must be written against what was actually built. |

No other edges: both reports (HLR-1, HLR-2) are built in the same component by
the same team on the same console reporting surface, so they form one epic
(boundary rule 2 — same component + same team + same logical change). CSV
export (HLR-3) is a presentation mode of the same report views and shares their
data structures and UI surface, so it is bundled rather than split. There are
no external dependencies, no new components to onboard (all three components
have architecture-context files and are Konflux-onboarded), and no open
questions, so no Investigation epics are needed.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Per-project idle-workbench report sourced from notebook controller activity tracking |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Stale pipeline-run report sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 (bundled) — CSV export is a presentation mode of the same report views built for HLR-1/HLR-2; it shares their data structures and UI surface, so a separate epic would build the same surface twice and is not independently schedulable | |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Documentation of reports and safe reclamation steps |

All four HLRs are covered; none are orphaned.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections:** the strategy omits the Impacted Teams table,
  Dependencies table, formal Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and
  non-functional requirements. Teams were derived from the architecture-context
  owning teams (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard). This is a strategy-quality gap,
  not a decomposition blocker.
- **Configurable-age default unspecified:** HLR-2's "configurable age" default
  value is an implementation detail for the team; captured as scope, not an
  unknown requiring investigation.
- **Passive-component assumption:** the decomposition relies on the strategy's
  premise that notebook-controller last-activity tracking and KFP run
  completion metadata are sufficient data sources. Architecture context
  corroborates both (last activity tracked per kernel through Jupyter server
  API probes; KFP v2 REST API with runs surfaced in the Dashboard), and the
  premise is verified as acceptance criteria on RHAISTRAT-9016-E001.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing.
